thread:
maria: Hey team — started getting 401 invalid_api_key in prod after a config push this morning. No code changes to auth flow, just a secret rotation. Error shows up in server logs: 

    HTTP 401 {
      "error": "invalid_api_key"
    }

  devon: Thanks — can you paste how the key is being read from the secret store? quick snippet is fine.

  maria: sure. using node, fetched from vault then passed into our http client like this: 

  ```js
  const key = process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY
  await fetch(url, {
    headers: { Authorization: `Apikey ${key}` }
  })
  ```

  maria: when I log typeof key it prints 'object' which is weird — vault team said they uploaded the new key as a JSON array by mistake.

  sam: ah that would do it — many http client libs (and proxies) will stringify arrays into comma-joined values. so header becomes `Apikey a,b,c` instead of the single token. API server treats that as malformed.

  devon: can you show an example of the raw header from one of the requests (curl -v from your pod or the ingress logs)? just redact the token part.

  maria: pasted ingress log snippet (redacted):

  `Authorization: Apikey ["sk_live_abc","def","ghi"]`

  devon: yep that's the problem. Redwood expects the apikey ASCII token exactly. extra brackets/commas/quotes will fail validation.

  sam: root cause summary: secret rotated but stored as a JSON array -> app read it as JS array -> header serialized -> 401. quick fix: convert to string when reading secret (e.g., process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY = secret[0]) or re-upload single string secret.

  maria: confirmed — updated the deployment to use secret[0] and requests are succeeding again. Thanks! :tada:

  devon: marking as resolved but also leaving a note for infra: ops-bot can you create a quick policy check so the secret uploader validates the type is string?

  ops-bot: created ticket INFRA-1729 to add validation and a CI check on secret format.

  sam: adding a small server-side improvement idea — clearer 401 error when header contains forbidden chars (like brackets/commas) so it's easier to debug next time. filing follow-up RFC.

  maria: great, thanks everyone.
